Dan volgt de derde étage en de topdagob. Van deze laatste waren reeds vroeger ettelijke stukken voorhanden t. w. van het lotuskussen, van den geornamenteerden rand en van de pijnakel; deze fragmenten, die sedert nog met enkele werden aangevuld, waren alleszins voldoende om de oorspronkelijke gedaante van de dagob te reconstrueeren.

Het eenige wat niet aan de hand van documenten kan worden vastgelegd, was de geheel verdwenen derde dakétage en Dr. Brandes, de geestelijke vader van het restauratie-ontwerp, heeft gemeend hiervoor een achtkantig grondplan te moeten aannemen. Hij heeft dit niet uitvoerig gemotiveerd en zich bepaald tot het wijzen op „de overeenstemming met andere oudheden”. Hoewel niet met name genoemd, is het duidelijk, dat het dak van Tjandi Kalasan hier het richtsnoer is geweest; hier is inderdaad de hoogste dakétage een achtkant, de overgangsvorm tusschen het onderliggende kwadraat met uitsprongen en de hooger gelegen cirkelvormige dagob.

Onder de kleinere bouwwerken vindt men een overeenkomstige ordonnantie bij een gedeelte der dwergtempeltjes van het Tjandi Sèwoe complex, terwijl bij de daken van Tjandi Loemboeng het achtkant reeds aanvangt bij de eerste étage.

Het is alleszins begrijpelijk dat men allereerst aan dat achtkant denkt, dat toch de logische schakel blijft tusschen kwadraat en cirkel. Toch zijn wij overtuigd dat hier een dwaling is ingeslopen en dat het grondplan der derde étage van Mendoet eene herhaling is geweest van dat der beide onderliggende verdiepingen, n. l. het vierkant met een uitsprong op elk der facen.

We meenen ons allereerst te moeten spiegelen aan de zoo nabijgelegen Tjandi Pawon, die in grondplan en profileering in veel opzichten een verkleinde copie kan genoemd worden van Mendoet (vergelijk plaat 59 Oudheidkundige Rapporten 1903). Bij Pawon heeft de bovenste étage inderdaad hetzelfde grondplan als de onderste.

pages.translation:
rings of decorative <term>dagobs</term> <gloss>miniature stupas</gloss> leaves no doubt, because the slots for them were still present here and there.

Then follows the third tier and the top <term>dagob</term>. Of the latter, several pieces were already available previously, namely of the lotus cushion, the ornamented edge, and the pinnacle; these fragments, which have since been supplemented with a few more, were quite sufficient to reconstruct the original shape of the <term>dagob</term>.

The only thing that cannot be established on the basis of documents was the completely disappeared third roof tier, and Dr. Brandes, the intellectual father of the restoration design, felt he had to assume an octagonal ground plan for this. He did not motivate this in detail and limited himself to pointing to "the agreement with other antiquities." Although not mentioned by name, it is clear that the roof of <term>Tjandi Kalasan</term> <gloss>an 8th-century Buddhist temple in Java</gloss> was the guiding principle here; there, the highest roof tier is indeed an octagon, the transitional form between the underlying square with projections and the higher circular <term>dagob</term>.

Among the smaller structures, one finds a corresponding arrangement in a part of the small temples of the <term>Tjandi Sèwoe</term> <gloss>a large 8th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple complex</gloss> complex, while for the roofs of <term>Tjandi Loemboeng</term> <gloss>a Javanese temple</gloss>, the octagon already begins at the first tier.

It is entirely understandable that one thinks first of that octagon, which after all remains the logical link between square and circle. Yet we are convinced that an error has crept in here and that the ground plan of the third tier of Mendoet was a repetition of that of the two underlying stories, namely the square with a projection on each of the faces.

We think we should first look to the nearby <term>Tjandi Pawon</term> <gloss>a small Buddhist temple near Borobudur</gloss>, which in ground plan and profiling can be called a reduced copy of Mendoet in many respects (compare plate 59 Archaeological Reports 1903). At Pawon, the top tier indeed has the same ground plan as the bottom one.

<summary>This page evaluates the architectural restoration of the Mendoet roof, debating whether the third tier was octagonal or square, and citing Tjandi Pawon as a comparative model.</summary>

Die namen zijn blijkbaar verbasterd; waaruit? is moeielijk te zeggen. De schuld ligt aan de afschijvers, die zelfs de namen van zulke bekende en doorluchtige wezens als de Jina's, zóó mishandeld hebben, dat ze grootendeels onherkenbaar zouden wezen, wist men niet van elders hoe ze luiden.

Zoo de eigennamen ons niet tot leiddraad kunnen strekken om bovengestelde vraag te beantwoorden, en 't gewenschte licht uit Indië niet opdaagt, blijft ons voorloopig niets over dan aan te nemen, dat de legende het werk is van een Javaanschen Mahâyânist, die eenige bestanddeelen van 't verhaal, o. a. de beschrijving der hellestraffen, en misschien alle, uit andere, ons onbekende bronnen geput, maar zelfstandig tot een geheel verwerkt heeft, en wel, naar het schijnt, met het bijoogmerk den Buddha Wairocana te verheerlijken, door hem te laten optreden als de verpersoonlijkte hoogste wijsheid en oppersten leeraar. Dat er op Java mythen over een reus Kuñjarakarṇa bestonden, die als varianten van de voorstelling in de legende kunnen beschouwd worden, kan men zien uit hetgeen v. D. TUUK meedeelt uit het zgn. Cantaka, een prozawerk, dat o. a. over allerlei mythen handelt. Daarin is Kuñjayakarṇa (sic) de eigennaam van iemand dien Ciwa in verzoeking liet brengen en in een Danuja veranderde; zijn vader heet Dumbajaya; als Danuja ijverig ascese verrichtende en den naam dragende van Darmasana, verlost hij Pûrṇawijaya uit de hel, na Yama en diens dienaren verslagen te hebben en herkrijgt later zijn menschelijke gedaante ¹).

De inhoud van de legende is, 't kort, als volgt. Zekere Yakṣa Kuñjarakarṇa wenscht in eene volgende vleeschwording een hoogeren staat te bereiken en oefent zich daarom als kluizenaar in zelfkastijding. In twijfel staande of hij als mensch dan wel als godheid zal verkiezen herboren te worden, besluit hij zich te laten onderrichten in den Dharma, de Wet, door Wairocana, den verheven Heer, wiens prediking, zooals hij vernomen heeft, door de overige Jina's, Bodhisatwa's en godheden met aandacht gevolgd wordt. Hij begeeft zich dan naar Bodhicitta, het verblijf van Wairocana en smeekt om onderricht te ontvangen. De genadige Heer belooft hem dit later te zullen geven, maar beveelt hem eerst naar 't rijk van Yama, den Vorst der Hel, te gaan en van dezen te hooren, waarom de boozen in de hel gepijnigd worden. De Yakṣa gehoorzaamt, en komt, niet zonder moeite, in de onderwereld, waar hij ruimschoots gelegenheid heeft te zien, welke gruwelijke folteringen

Those names are clearly corrupted; from what? is difficult to say. The fault lies with the copyists, who have so mistreated even the names of such well-known and illustrious beings as the <term>Jina's</term> <gloss>victorious ones/Buddhas</gloss> that they would be largely unrecognizable if one did not know from elsewhere how they are pronounced.

If proper names cannot serve as a guide for us to answer the question posed above, and the desired light from India does not appear, there remains for the time being nothing for us but to assume that the legend is the work of a Javanese <term>Mahâyânist</term> <gloss>follower of Mahayana Buddhism</gloss>, who has drawn some components of the story, among others the description of hell punishments, and perhaps all of them, from other unknown sources, but has processed them independently into a whole, and indeed, as it seems, with the secondary intent to glorify the Buddha <term>Wairocana</term> <gloss>the cosmic Buddha</gloss> by having him act as the personified highest wisdom and supreme teacher. That myths about a giant <term>Kuñjarakarṇa</term> existed on Java, which can be considered as variants of the representation in the legend, can be seen from what <term>v. D. TUUK</term> communicates from the so-called <term>Cantaka</term>, a prose work that, among other things, deals with all kinds of myths. In it, <term>Kuñjayakarṇa</term> (sic) is the proper name of someone whom <term>Ciwa</term> <gloss>Shiva</gloss> let be tempted and changed into a <term>Danuja</term> <gloss>demon</gloss>; his father is named <term>Dumbajaya</term>; as a <term>Danuja</term> zealously performing asceticism and bearing the name of <term>Darmasana</term>, he delivers <term>Pûrṇawijaya</term> from hell after having defeated <term>Yama</term> and his servants, and later regains his human form ¹).

The content of the legend is, in short, as follows. A certain <term>Yakṣa</term> <term>Kuñjarakarṇa</term> wishes to reach a higher state in a subsequent incarnation and therefore practices self-mortification as a hermit. In doubt whether he will choose to be reborn as a human or as a deity, he decides to have himself instructed in the <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>the Law/Truth</gloss> by <term>Wairocana</term>, the exalted Lord, whose preaching, as he has heard, is followed with attention by the remaining <term>Jina's</term>, <term>Bodhisatwa's</term> <gloss>beings destined for enlightenment</gloss>, and deities. He then betakes himself to <term>Bodhicitta</term>, the residence of <term>Wairocana</term>, and begs to receive instruction. The merciful Lord promises to give him this later but commands him first to go to the realm of <term>Yama</term>, the Prince of Hell, and to hear from him why the wicked are tormented in hell. The <term>Yakṣa</term> obeys and comes, not without difficulty, into the underworld, where he has ample opportunity to see what terrible tortures

De dienaren van Yama waren echter nog niet tevreden; daarom werden (de boozen) op nieuw gefolterd, geslagen met ijzeren knotsen zoo dik als een Pinangstam. Anderen werden gestoken met ijzeren spiesen van 10 vadem lengte, bij honderden te gelijk. Hoe zagen zij er uit? Als doorregen sprinkhanen. Zij zochten in allerijl een goed heenkomen, vouwden eerbiedig de handen en hieven een luid <note>37</note> geschreeuw aan, jammerlijk zeggende: ,,Ach, groote Heeren, dienaren van Yama! hebt medelijden met mij; laat mij leven en herboren worden op aarde; leert mij wat behoorlijk of onbehoorlijk <note>38</note> is, opdat ik de zonde kunne verzaken, als gehoorzame dienaar der Paṇḍita's (geestelijken), en de werken van weldadigheid volbrengen; thans daarentegen oogst <note>39</note> ik de vruchten der dwaasheid''. Dat was een geschrei! een geroep van ach en wee! ,,Al te vuig is het kwaad dat jij bedreven hebt <note>40</note>, is niet? daarvan kun je in gemoede verzekerd zijn. Hoe zou ik je kunnen vergunnen om wedergeboren <note>41</note> te worden? De geheele wereld toch zou te niet gaan, alsook de Wet (d. i. de orde der natuur), de tijdregeling, de natuur der dingen, de wereldverzaking, de vroomheid, de betamelijkheid, alwat recht is. Waartoe zou je dan hierna wedergeboren worden? De wereld <note>43</note> zou immers door jou als het ware in vuur en vlam gezet worden, ten gevolge van je vroegere verwatenheid. Ook waar je inhalig en hebt herhaaldelijk onschuldige menschen gedood. Thans is het kwaad dat je gedaan hebt, een ijzeren spies geworden, dat je lichaam bedreigt als loon van de dwaasheid <note>44</note> waaraan jij je schuldig gemaakt hebt. Dat alles is je verdiende loon, jij slechtaard!'' Plots hoorde men 't geluid van steken; plof! plof! voortdurend werden zij met een ijzeren knots geslagen: plots! klets! klets! overal zag men punten uitsteken. Zoo gingen de dienaren van Yama te werk, terwijl zij al de boozen pijnigden <note>45</note>, die van pijn kermden. Daarna werden zij opgehangen en (onder hen) werd vuur aangelegd. Toen kreeg Kuñjarakarṇa de boozen in 't oog: hij stond stil, pijnlijk aangedaan, bij den aanblik der boozen, die door de dienaren van Yama getuchtigd werden. Kuñjarakarṇa voelde een snerpende pijn in zijn ziel: het was hem alsof hem de lichaamsgewrichten in stukken gesneden werden. Het was alsof hij biddend de handen ophief voor Bhatâra Wairocana, met de woorden: ,,Aho namo Bhatâra! namaḥ Ċiwâya''. (hulde o Heer! hulde aan Ċiwa)! Grenzeloos is de genade des Heeren jegens mij, dat hij mij beval naar Yama's te gaan om te aanschouwen wat aan alle boozen bereid is. Nu eerst begrijp ik

The servants of Yama, however, were not yet satisfied; therefore (the wicked) were tortured anew, beaten with iron clubs as thick as an areca palm trunk. Others were pierced with iron spears of 10 fathoms length, by the hundreds at a time. How did they look? Like threaded locusts. They sought a safe haven in a hurry, folded their hands reverently, and raised a loud <note>³⁷) piercing.</note> cry, lamenting, saying: "Ach, great Lords, servants of Yama! Have pity on me; let me live and be reborn on earth; teach me what is proper or improper <note>³⁸) wrong.</note>, so that I may renounce sin, as an obedient servant of the <term>Paṇḍita's</term> <gloss>priests/learned men</gloss>, and perform works of charity; now, on the contrary, I reap <note>³⁹) harvest.</note> the fruits of foolishness." That was a wailing! A crying of oh and woe! "Too foul is the evil that you have committed <note>⁴⁰) done.</note>, is it not? Of that you can be convinced in all honesty. How could I permit you to be reborn <note>⁴¹) reincarnated.</note>? For the whole world would perish, as well as the Law (i.e., the order of nature), the chronology, the nature of things, world-renunciation, piety, decency, everything that is right. For what would you then be reborn hereafter? The world <note>⁴³) the universe.</note> would indeed be set on fire by you, as it were, as a result of your former arrogance. Also, where you were greedy and have repeatedly killed innocent people. Now the evil that you have done has become an iron spear, which threatens your body as a reward for the foolishness <note>⁴⁴) stupidity.</note> of which you have made yourself guilty. That is all your earned reward, you villain!" Suddenly one heard the sound of piercing; plop! plop! Constantly they were beaten with an iron club: plop! smack! smack! Everywhere one saw points sticking out. Thus the servants of Yama went to work, while they tormented <note>⁴⁵) punished.</note> all the wicked, who moaned in pain. Thereafter they were hung up and fire was lit (beneath them). Then Kuñjarakarṇa caught sight of the wicked: he stood still, painfully affected by the sight of the wicked, who were chastised by the servants of Yama. Kuñjarakarṇa felt a stinging pain in his soul: it was to him as if his body joints were cut to pieces. It was as if he were raising his hands in prayer to <term>Bhatâra Wairocana</term>, with the words: "Aho namo Bhatâra! namaḥ Ċiwâya!" (Homage, o Lord! Homage to <term>Ċiwa</term> <gloss>Shiva</gloss>)! Boundless is the grace of the Lord towards me, that he commanded me to go to Yama's (realm) to witness what is prepared for all the wicked. Nu echter heeft het korter geduurd. Wat is de reden daarvan? Wees zoo goed en deel mij de reden daarvan mede, Meester.” — „Och, mijn zoon Bhaṭâra Yamâdhipati en gij alle vier behoeders der windstreken! het is zeer goed van u, dat gij zoo vrij zijt te vragen naar [de reden van] de voorgeschiedenis van Pûrṇawijaya. Nu, luistert dan goed. Er is een oord, Bhûmimaṇḍala genaamd. (Daar leefde een man) 135) die veel zilver, goud, edelgesteenten en knechten bezat. Hij heette Muladara. Hij bracht goede werken tot stand: fonteinbakken, rustplaatsen voor reizigers, platte steenen om op te zitten. Hij had een bouwmeester die zijn medehelper was in 't doen van goede werken, Kirnagata geheeten. Deze was zijn medehelper in liefdewerken. Er was een (ander) oord, Tapalinada genaamd. Daar woonde een man die zeer behoeftig was, geen kind noch aardsche goederen had, Utsâhadharma geheeten, hij met zijn vrouw. De naam zijner beminde gade was Sudharmâ. Zij leefden in zeer kommerlijke omstandigheden, maar zij waren zachtmoedig, vroom, minzaam in hun woorden, vriendelijk van gelaat. Zij waren uitermate weldadig, want zij hadden de heilige Wet gehoord. Daarom deden zij mede aan goede werken; zij strekten de hand niet uit, zonder telkens daarmede aalmoezen te schenken aan de voorbijgangers, wat zij vergezeld deden gaan van blijmoedigheid, vromen zin, minzame woorden en een vriendelijk gelaat. Nu trof het zoo, dat zij goede werken deden nabij de plaats waar Muladara goede werken verrichtte. Dit gaf aanleiding dat Muladara Utsâhadharma uitschold, zeggende: „Hei, jij Utsâhadharma! jij, slechtaard, armzalige ellendeling! 136) waarom toch doe jij goede werken nabij de plaats waar ik goede werken verricht? Jij bent een smeerlap, een laag schepsel. De goede werken die jij doet zijn niet waard een twint. Wacht je daarom wel, om naar mij te kijken als ik goede werken volbreng. Ik slacht buffels, koeien, wilde zwijnen; (onthaal op) palmwijn en rijst, waaraan tal van menschen, zooveel als er van eten, zich verzadigen. Maar jij, kleuter! verbeeldt je heel wat te zijn en tegen mij op te kunnen met je goede werken. Je houdt vol met zoo onbeschaamd te zijn, kleuter, om naar mij te kijken? Ga heen, hel ver weg! to worship Wairocana, namely: Indra, Yama, Waruṇa, Kuwera, Waiçrawaṇa; all greeted the Lord respectfully. Then <term>Yamādhipati</term> asked the Lord: "Oh, Lord and Master! What is the cause that Pūrṇawijaya has been called back to life by you? After all, he was originally destined to be boiled in the cauldron for a hundred years. Now, however, it has lasted a shorter time. What is the reason for that? Be so kind as to communicate the reason to me, Master." — "Oh, my son Bhaṭāra <term>Yamādhipati</term> and you all four guardians of the wind directions! It is very good of you that you are so free to ask about [the reason for] the history of Pūrṇawijaya. Now, listen well. There is a place called <term>Bhūmimaṇḍala</term>. (There lived a man) <note>135</note> who possessed much silver, gold, precious stones, and servants. He was called Muladara. He brought about good works: fountains, rest stops for travelers, flat stones to sit on. He had a master builder who was his helper in doing good works, called Kirnagata. This one was his helper in works of charity. There was another place called <term>Tapalinada</term>. There lived a man who was very needy, had neither children nor earthly goods, called Utsâhadharma, he with his wife. The name of his beloved spouse was Sudharmâ. They lived in very miserable circumstances, but they were gentle, pious, affable in their words, friendly of face. They were extremely charitable, for they had heard the holy Law. Therefore they participated in good works; they did not stretch out their hands without always bestowing alms upon passersby, which they did accompanied by cheerfulness, a pious mind, affable words, and a friendly face. Now it happened that they did good works near the place where Muladara performed good works. This gave cause for Muladara to scold Utsâhadharma, saying: "Hey, you Utsâhadharma! You, evildoer, miserable wretch! <note>136</note> Why do you perform good works near the place where I perform good works? You are a scoundrel, a base creature. The good works you do are not worth a dime. Therefore, be careful not to look at me when I perform good works. I slaughter buffaloes, cows, wild boars; (I provide) palm wine and rice, with which many people, as many as eat from it, sate themselves. But you, little child! Imagine yourself to be quite something and able to compete with me in your good works. You persist in being so impudent, child, to look at me? Go away, get far away! Get yourself away from here!" — Thus spoke Muladara, scolding Utsâhadharma. Then Utsâhadharma said to

92) Of hier onder *Yogîçwara* uitsluitend Wairocana verstaan moet worden, is niet duidelijk; vgl. Verh. blz. 17. De zinsnede van *ndah ya iki* enz. tot aan *wkas i taṅan ira* maakt den indruk van ingeschoven te zijn.

93) L. *padudwan tika*.

The depiction of the womb, <term>kukṣi</term>, as a jewel-box occurs frequently in Buddhist scriptures; among others <term>Mahâvastu</term> I, 213; II, 16, where it is said that the Bodhisatwa rests in the <term>kukṣi</term> of Mâyâ like a beryl jewel in a small crystal box; compare <term>Lalita-Wistara</term> 76.

77) It is difficult to say what is meant by this gibberish.

78) Actually "cleft," because <term>gaga</term>, poor spelling for <term>gangang</term>, is Javanese <term>goṅgang</term>, Dayak <term>gagaṅgang</term>.

79) Compare Javanese <term>kopah-kopah</term>.

80) <term>Pula</term>, imperfect spelling for <term>pulaṅ</term>.

81) The text is clearly in disarray; I read: <term>sy Adikumára ṅaranta, saṅ hyaṅ Saṅgraha ṅaraṅ ajinta</term>.

83) <term>Mánayanaya</term> is, I suppose, a variant of or error for <term>maniyaniya</term>.

84) Most names of unclean substances in the body are hopelessly spoiled; <term>koṭaka</term> and <term>kuṭaka</term> I have taken conjecturally as Sanskrit <term>koṭha</term> and <term>koṣṭha</term>, <term>gwaṭaka</term> as <term>gúthaka</term>. <term>Candaka</term> perhaps for Sanskrit <term>syanda</term>, rheumatic substance.

87) <term>Rusa-rusi</term> for <term>ruṅsaṅ-ruṅsiṅ</term>.

88) Read <term>ndan</term>, and a little further <term>kasihana</term>.

89) Read <term>ahning</term>, <term>ahwa</term> (i.e., <term>aho</term>). The root word <term>ho</term> corresponds to the Bisaya <term>hao</term>, of which <term>haoan</term>, to purify; <term>haohao</term>, to refresh oneself.

90) Read <term>wari</term>.

91) This resembles <term>Wedânta</term>; compare Treatise before page 17. The <term>kleça</term>s <gloss>defilements/hindrances</gloss> are, according to the conception that shines through in this place, the obstacles innate to man to penetrate to the highest truth.

92) Whether here under <term>Yogîçwara</term> <gloss>Lord of Yoga</gloss> exclusively Wairocana is to be understood, is not clear; compare Treatise page 17. The phrase from <term>ndah ya iki</term> etc. up to <term>wkas i taṅan ira</term> makes the impression of having been inserted.

93) Read <term>padudwan tika</term>.

<margin>
Truth
</margin>
within the Essence of God. That is the phrase mentioned: "There is no god but God" <note>Arabic: La ilaha illa Allah</note>. "There is no god" is within the Essence; remember that there is no existence except the existence of God. "There is no god but God" is the place where it is spoken. "There is no god but God" is the end of words, and the Essence of God is Eternal. The place where one is commanded to say "Ya Hu, Ya Hu" <note>O He, O He</note> is where one feels the manifestation. Speak and remember, outwardly and inwardly, that before the state of God there is no existence, except for the existence of God. "There is no god but God" negates the existence of the self, so that only the existence of the One and Eternal God remains. That is the secret of nothingness being directed toward the Essence. This is called Negation <note>Arabic: Nafi</note> and Affirmation <note>Arabic: Isbat</note>. Negation is the first meaning; Affirmation means honoring the Eternal Essence of God and the state of God. If in these words there is still duality, then it is not a true Negation and Affirmation. In perfect words, there is neither Negation nor Affirmation. This point is fixed in the <term>ayan thabitah</term> <gloss>fixed archetypes</gloss>, called eternal stability. This is within the "tasting" <note>Arabic: dhawq</note>.

Know that the indication of remembrance <note>Arabic: dhikr</note> enters here from all the saints <note>Arabic: wali</note> of God the Exalted. All of them take the path of contemplation <note>Arabic: muraqabah</note>, remembrance <note>Arabic: dhikr</note>, orientation <note>Arabic: tawajjuh</note>, and witnessing <note>Arabic: mushahadah</note>, so that their actions become clear to all the saints of God by following this path. The indication of this remembrance is that the phrase <term>La ilaha illa Allah</term> is spoken with the tongue and strengthened in the heart, meaning there is no existence for them except the existence of God the Exalted. Whoever knows and considers their existence as the existence of God the Exalted, that is the one whose gnosis <note>Arabic: ma'rifat</note> is perfect. As for the indication of contemplation <note>Arabic: muraqabah</note>, it is the excuse <note>meaning the means</note> by which one's own existence is firmly negated when stating "La ilaha" <note>There is no god</note>, and one's existence is affirmed as the Essence of God the Exalted when stating "illa Allah" <note>except God</note>.

<column-break/>

<margin>
Truth
</margin>
As for the indication of orientation <note>Arabic: tawajjuh</note>, the eye of the heart should be directed toward the existence of the self as the Essence of God, while simultaneously having nothing else in that focus. Let there be nothing in the heart except the name of God the Exalted, and remember the Essence of His existence. As for the indication of witnessing <note>Arabic: mushahadah</note>, it is to realize that the fixed archetypes <note>Arabic: ayan thabitah</note> are not other than the external archetypes <note>Arabic: ayan kharijiyyah</note>. This is the realization. When both are seen as one, the path of seeing one's own existence as the existence of God the Exalted is made clear, as taught by the spiritual guide <note>Arabic: murshid</note>. In the path of witnessing, the heart is detached from all other paths of witnessing because it is the witnessing of the Essence of God the Exalted. This is like the indication of the saint of God regarding "annihilation in God" <note>Arabic: fana' fillah</note> and "subsistence in God" <note>Arabic: baqa' billah</note>. If one sees anything else, that is the state of a servant, but success comes from God the Exalted. This is the end of the science of the Gnosis of God the Exalted, God willing. Whoever has obtained this perfect science of Gnosis of God the Exalted from a guide who is perfect and perfecting <note>Arabic: kamil mukammil</note>, let them not speak of this science of Gnosis to those who are not worthy. It should only be shown to those who are fit for it. If you show this science of Gnosis to those who are not its people, you will surely be distanced by God the Exalted, and remain among the common folk at the level of the ignorant. Such a person is a servant who does not truly praise God the Exalted, nor the Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, who governs the Kaaba of God. By God, and in God, let it be so. This marks the completion of the book "The Pearl of Realities" <note>Arabic: Durrat al-Daqaiq</note> by the master Sheikh Shamsuddin ibn Abdullah al-Sumatrani.

<summary>This page details the practice of Dhikr, Muraqabah, and Mushahadah, emphasizing the negation of self and affirmation of God's existence, concluding with a warning to keep these teachings secret.</summary>
<keywords>La ilaha illa Allah, Nafi, Isbat, Muraqabah, Mushahadah, Fana, Baqa, Shamsuddin al-Sumatrani</keywords>

<margin>As for the level of Oneness <term>Ahadiyyah</term>, it is the level of the Essence of God <term>Zat Allah</term>; the Jewel is without attributes and without any considerations. The Essence of God is pure from all considerations.</margin>

To Him who was not... the heavens and the earth... not twice... not... when the seven layers of heaven and earth were created...

<margin>Oneness <term>Ahadiyyah</term></margin>

->Oneness <term>Ahadiyyah</term><-

<margin>The reality of Life <term>Hayat</term> resides in our body; life is that which is close to the Life of God, for that attribute is like the sun with its rays; that is the expression of the Abstract Attribute <term>Sifat Ma'nuwiyyah</term>.</margin>

Life <term>Hayat</term>

<margin>The reality of Knowledge <term>Ilmu</term> in our body is the Knowledge of God; it is close to the Knowing of God, for that attribute is like the sun with its rays; that is the expression of the Abstract Attribute.</margin>

Knowledge <term>Ilmu</term>

<margin>The attribute of Will <term>Iradat</term> resides in our self; it is close to our will being with the Will of God.</margin>

Will <term>Iradat</term>

<margin>The reality of Power <term>Qudrat</term> in our body is the Power of God; it is close to the Power of God, for that attribute is like the sun with its rays; that is the expression of the Abstract Attribute.</margin>

Power <term>Qudrat</term>

<margin>The reality of Hearing <term>Sama'</term> in our body is the Hearing of God; it is close to the Hearing of God, for that attribute is like the sun with its rays; that is the expression of the Abstract Attribute.</margin>

Hearing <term>Sama'</term>

<margin>The reality of Vision <term>Basar</term> in our body is the Vision of God; it is close to the Vision of God, for that attribute is like the sun with its rays; that is the expression of the Abstract Attribute.</margin>

Vision <term>Basar</term>

<margin>The reality of Speech <term>Kalam</term> in our body is the Speech of God; it is close to the Speech of God, for that attribute is like the sun with its rays; that is the expression of the Abstract Attribute.</margin>

Speech <term>Kalam</term>

<column-break/>

<margin>Peace be upon him, I bear witness to the eternal...</margin>

->Greater than the three Acts<-

The Sacred Law <term>Syariat</term> is my word; the Path <term>Tarekat</term> is my action.
The Reality <term>Hakikat</term> for us becomes the world.
And the Reality...
And the Reality is my station; Gnosis <term>Makrifat</term> is my capital.

<margin>The Sacred Law is for us to know; Gnosis is our head.</margin>

->The Source of the Light of the Eyes<-

Such is the arrangement of the World of Spirits <term>Alam Arwah</term>, the World of Images <term>Alam Mithal</term>, the World of Bodies <term>Alam Ajsam</term>, and the World of Man <term>Alam Insan</term>.
Existence between two non-existences is a manifestation between two Presences.

<margin>The reality of man is the Spirit, the World of Images, the World of Spirits, and the World of Man.</margin>

As for this existence... purity between...
And God knows best.

<margin>As for the level of Unity <term>Wahdiyyah</term>, it is the level of the Attributes of God the Exalted; the Jewel is without any considerations. The Essence of God is pure from all considerations.</margin>

pages.translation:
<margin></margin>
Permanence <term>Baqa</term>: The Essence of Allah the Exalted is Permanent/Everlasting. He is Eternal and will never perish. All Attributes of Allah are Permanent. Everything other than the Essence and Attributes of Allah will perish. The Permanence of Allah is through His Essence alone. Allah knows best.
</margin>

<margin></margin>
Difference from Created Things <term>Mukhalafah lil-hawadith</term>: The Essence of Allah is different from all originated things. The Attributes of Allah are different from all originated things. The Acts of Allah are different from all originated things. This difference is through the Essence of Allah alone. Allah knows best.
</margin>

<margin></margin>
Self-Subsistence <term>Qiyamuhu binafsihi</term>: The Essence of Allah stands by itself. He does not require a place nor does He require a creator. All Attributes of Allah stand through the Essence of Allah alone. Allah knows best.
</margin>

<margin></margin>
Oneness <term>Wahdaniyah</term>: The Essence of Allah is One in Essence, One in Attributes, and One in Acts. There are not two Essences, two Attributes, or two Acts. The Oneness of Allah is through His Essence alone. Allah knows best.
</margin>

-> Know <-
There is the time of Allah, who creates all that is created. The world is originated <term>baharu</term>. This originated world and everything in it exists through the Eternal Power <term>Qudrat</term> and Eternal Will <term>Iradat</term> of Allah the Exalted. Allah knows best.

-> Knowledge <-
The Essence of Allah is Knowing <term>Alim</term>. He knows all that is Necessary, Impossible, and Possible. The Necessary is the Essence and Attributes of Allah. The Impossible is any partner for Allah. The Possible is the entire universe: the earth, the heavens, and everything within them. Allah knows best.

<column-break/>

### Life <term>Hayat</term>
This means living. Life is an eternal attribute that sustains the form of life of the prophets, angels, humans, jinn, devils, crawling animals, flying animals, insects, aquatic animals, plants that grow on the earth, and trees both large and small. All of these possess an originated life created by Allah the Exalted. The Life of Allah the Exalted is Eternal <term>Qadim</term>, without beginning and without end. The Life of Allah is not through a soul, nor through the ego <term>nafs</term>, nor through blood, nor through cold or heat, nor through steam, nor through wind, nor through breathing air. All of those are originated attributes created by Allah the Exalted. The Life of Allah the Exalted is an eternal attribute that sustains the life of the Essence of Allah and all His eternal Attributes. The Life of Allah the Exalted is different from the life of all originated things. Allah knows best.

### Knowledge <term>Ilmu</term>
This means knowing. Knowledge is an eternal attribute that eternally manifests all that is Necessary, Impossible, and Possible. The Knowledge of Allah the Exalted is Eternal, without beginning and without end. The Knowledge of Allah the Exalted is not through thought, nor through the intellect <term>aql</term>, nor through reading, nor through learning, nor through recognition, nor through taste, nor through smell, nor through hearing, nor through sight. All of those are originated attributes created by Allah the Exalted. The Knowledge of Allah the Exalted is an eternal attribute that eternally manifests the Essence of Allah and all His eternal Attributes. The Knowledge of Allah the Exalted is different from the knowledge of all originated things. Allah knows best.

فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ بِإِحْسَانٍ ذَلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَرَ
حْمَةٌ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصَاصِ
حَيَاةٌ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ
أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْرًا الْوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَ
بِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ بَعْدَ مَا سَمِعَهُ
فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ فَمَنْ خَافَ
مِنْ مُوصٍ جَنَفًا أَوْ إِثْمًا فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ
غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ
عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ
فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ
وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ فَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ
خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ هُدًى لِلنَّاسِ
وَبَيِّنَاتٍ مِنَ الْهُدَى وَالْفُرْقَانِ فَمَنْ شَهِدَ مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ
فَلْيَصُمْهُ وَمَنْ كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ

<column-break/>

مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ
وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ
تَشْكُرُونَ وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ
يَرْشُدُونَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَى نِسَائِكُمْ
هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَهُنَّ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ
تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ
وَابْتَغُوا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ
لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا
الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَا
جِدِ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ
آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ
وَتُدْلُوا بِهَا إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا فَرِيقًا مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ
بِالْإِثْمِ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ
قُلْ هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَالْحَجِّ وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا

then there should be a suitable follow-up and payment to him with kindness. This is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy. But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment. And there is for you in legal retribution <note>original: "al-qisas"</note> saving of life, O you of understanding, that you may become righteous. Prescribed for you when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, is that he should make a bequest for the parents and near relatives according to what is acceptable—a duty upon the righteous. Then whoever alters the bequest after he has heard it—the sin is only upon those who have altered it. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. But if one fears from the testator aslanting toward some or a sin and amends the matter between the parties, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous. Fasting for a fixed number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days are to be made up. And upon those who are able to fast but with hardship, a ransom of feeding a needy person is required. And whoever volunteers excess good, it is better for him. And to fast is better for you, if you only knew. The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and the criterion. So whoever sights the new moon of the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey—then an equal number 

<column-break/>

of other days. God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and wants for you to complete the period and to glorify God for that to which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful. And when My servants ask you concerning Me—indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be rightly guided. It has been made lawful for you on the night of the fasts to go to your wives. They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them. God knows that you used to deceive yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which God has decreed for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread of night. Then complete the fast until the sunset. And do not have relations with them while you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His ordinances to the people that they may become righteous. And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it as bribes to the rulers in order that you might consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin while you know it. They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for <term>Hajj</term>." And it is not piety that you enter

يبلغ الكتاب اجله واعلموا ان الله يعلم ما في انفسكم فاحذروه
واعلموا ان الله غفور حليم لا جناح عليكم ان طلقتم النساء
ما لم تمسوهن او تفرضوا لهن فريضة ومتعوهن على
الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره متاعا بالمعروف وحقا على
المحسنين وان طلقتموهن من قبل ان تمسوهن وقد فرضتم
لهن فريضة فنصف ما فرضتم الا ان يعفون او يعفوا الذي
بيده عقدة النكاح وان تعفوا اقرب للتقوى ولا تنسوا الفضل
بينكم ان الله بما تعملون بصير حافظوا على الصلوات والصلوة
الوسطى وقوموا لله قانتين فان خفتم فرجالا او ركبانا فاذا
امنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون والذين
يتوفون منكم ويذرون ازواجا وصية لازواجهم
متاعا الى الحول غير اخراج فان خرجن فلا جناح
عليكم فيما فعلن في انفسهن من معروف والله عزيز حكيم
وللمطلقات متاع بالمعروف وحقا على المتقين كذلك يبين
الله لكم اياته لعلكم تعقلون الم تر الى الذين خرجوا من
ديارهم وهم الوف حذر الموت فقال لهم الله موتوا ثم

<column-break/>

احياهم ان الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن اكثر الناس
لا يشكرون وقاتلوا في سبيل الله واعلموا ان الله سميع
عليم من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه
له اضعافا كثيرة والله يقبض ويبسط واليه ترجعون
الم تر الى الملا من بني اسرائيل من بعد موسى اذ قالوا
لنبي لهم ابعث لنا ملكا نقاتل في سبيل الله قال هل عسيتم
ان كتب عليكم القتال الا تقاتلوا قالوا وما لنا الا نقاتل
في سبيل الله وقد اخرجنا من ديارنا وابنائنا فلما كتب
عليهم القتال تولوا الا قليلا منهم والله عليم بالظالمين
فقال لهم نبيهم ان الله قد بعث لكم طالوت ملكا قالوا
انى يكون له الملك علينا ونحن احق بالملك منه ولم
يؤت سعة من المال قال ان الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده
بسطة في العلم والجسم والله يؤتي ملكه من يشاء والله
واسع عليم وقال لهم نبيهم ان ايه ملكه ان ياتيكم التابوت
فيه سكينة من ربكم وبقية مما ترك ال موسى وال هارون
تحمله الملائكة ان في ذلك لاية لكم ان كنتم مؤمنين

pages.translation:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta> until the written decree reaches its prescribed term. And know that God knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that God is Forgiving and Forbearing. There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not yet touched them or specified for them an obligatory bridal gift <note>original: "faridatan", a mandatory marriage portion</note>. But provide for them—the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means—a provision in an equitable manner. This is a duty upon those who do good. And if you divorce them before you have touched them, but you have already specified for them an obligation, then give them half of what you specified, unless they forego it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract <note>original: "’uqdat al-nikah", referring to the husband or guardian</note> foregoes it. And to forego is closer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between yourselves. Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do. Maintain with care the prayers and the middle prayer <note>original: "al-salat al-wusta", often identified as the afternoon prayer</note> and stand before God in devout obedience. And if you fear <note>danger</note>, then pray while walking or riding. But when you are secure, then remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know. And those of you who die and leave wives behind should make a will for their wives of maintenance for a year without turning them out. But if they leave of their own accord, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an equitable manner. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. And for divorced women is a provision in an equitable manner, a duty upon the righteous. Thus God makes clear to you His verses so that you may understand. Have you not considered those who left their homes in the thousands, fearing death? God said to them, "Die"; then 

<column-break/>

He restored them to life. Indeed, God is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful. And fight in the cause of God and know that God is Hearing and Knowing. Who is it that will lend God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is God who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned. Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after the time of Moses when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king that we may fight in the cause of God"? He said, "Would you perhaps, if fighting were ordained for you, refrain from fighting?" They said, "And why should we not fight in the cause of God when we have been driven out from our homes and our children?" But when fighting was ordained for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, God has sent Saul <note>original: "Talut"</note> to you as a king." They said, "How can he have kingship over us while we are more worthy of kingship than him and he has not been given an abundance of wealth?" He said, "Indeed, God has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature. And God grants His sovereignty to whom He wills. And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing." And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the chest <note>original: "al-tabut", the Ark of the Covenant</note> will come to you, in which is reassurance <note>original: "sakinah", divine tranquility</note> from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers."

<summary>This page contains verses 235 to 248 of Surah Al-Baqarah, covering legislation on divorce, maintenance for widows, and the middle prayer, followed by the narrative of the Children of Israel requesting a king and the appointment of Saul.</summary>

فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي
الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ . قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لَسْتُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ حَتَّىٰ
تُقِيمُوا التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنجِيلَ وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ
كَثِيرًا مِّنْهُم مَّا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًا فَلَا تَأْسَ
عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ . إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئُونَ
وَالنَّصَارَىٰ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَا
خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ . لَقَدْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ
وَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ رُسُلًا كُلَّمَا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَىٰ أَنفُسُهُمْ
فَرِيقًا كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقًا يَقْتُلُونَ . وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ
فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا ثُمَّ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا
كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ . لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ
قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَقَالَ الْمَسِيحُ يَا بَنِي
إِسْرَائِيلَ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ مَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ
فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَاهُ النَّارُ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ

<column-break/>

أَنصَارٍ . لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَاثَةٍ وَمَا
مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِن لَّمْ يَنتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ
كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ . أَفَلَا يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ
وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ . مَّا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ
قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ
الطَّعَامَ انظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآيَاتِ ثُمَّ انظُرْ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ .
قُلْ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا
وَلَا نَفْعًا وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ . قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ
لَا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا أَهْوَاءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ
ضَلُّوا مِن قَبْلُ وَأَضَلُّوا كَثِيرًا وَضَلُّوا عَن سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ . لُعِنَ
الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُودَ وَعِيسَى ابْنِ
مَرْيَمَ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا وَّكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ . كَانُوا لَا يَتَنَا
هَوْنَ عَن مُّنكَرٍ فَعَلُوهُ لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ . تَرَىٰ كَثِيرًا
مِّنْهُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَبِئْسَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ أَنفُسُهُمْ

<vocab>المسيح, مريم, بني إسرائيل, التوراة, الإنجيل, كفروا, آمنوا</vocab>
pages.translation:
<meta>continues from previous page: judge between them or turn away from them.</meta>
...then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people. Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people. Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are [standing] on nothing until you uphold the <term>Torah</term> <gloss>Law of Moses</gloss> and the <term>Gospel</term> <gloss>Message of Jesus</gloss> and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people. Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians—whoever believed in God and the Last Day and worked righteousness—no fear shall there be upon them, nor shall they grieve. We had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party [of messengers] they denied, and another party they killed. And they thought there would be no <term>fitnah</term> <gloss>trial or consequence</gloss>, so they became blind and deaf. Then God turned to them in forgiveness; then [again] many of them became blind and deaf. And God is Seeing of what they do. They have certainly disbelieved who say, "God is the Messiah, the son of Mary" while the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with God—God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any

<column-break/>

helpers. They have certainly disbelieved who say, "God is the third of three." And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment. Will they not repent to God and ask His forgiveness? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded. Say, "Do you worship besides God that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit? And God is the Hearing, the Knowing." Say, "O People of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion beyond the truth and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and misled many and have strayed from the soundness of the way." Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed. They used not to prevent one another from wrongdoing that they did. Wretched was that which they were doing. You see many of them becoming allies of those who disbelieved. Wretched is that which their souls have sent forth for them...

حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به
وهم على صلوتهم يحافظون ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا
أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال
سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون
في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطوا أيديهم أخرجوا
أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون
على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون ولقد جئتمونا
فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم
وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم
الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع
بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون إن الله فالق الحب والنوى
يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم
الله فأنى تؤفكون فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل
سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير
العزيز العليم وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا

<column-break/>

بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون
وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع
قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون وهو الذي أنزل
من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا
منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها
قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون
والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر
وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون وجعلوا لله
شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم
سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون بديع السموات والأرض أنى
يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء
وهو بكل شيء عليم ذلكم الله ربكم لا
إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل
لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف
الخبير قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه

pages.translation:
<meta>continues from previous page: then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people. And those who fear God are not held accountable for the disbelievers at all, but this is a reminder that perhaps they will fear Him. And leave those who take their religion as amusement and play and whom the worldly life has deluded. But remind with the Quran, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it has earned; it will have other than God no protector and no intercessor. And if it should offer every ransom, it would not be taken from it. Those are the ones who are given to destruction for what they have earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve. Say, "Shall we invoke instead of God that which neither benefits us nor harms us and be turned back on our heels after God has guided us? Like one whom the devils have enticed to bewilderment on the earth, who has companions calling him to guidance, saying, 'Come to us.'" Say, "Indeed, the guidance of God is the only guidance; and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds. And to establish prayer and fear Him." And it is He to whom you will be gathered. And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the day He says, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion on the Day the Horn is blown. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted. And remember when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error." And thus did we show Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth that he would be among the certain in faith. So when the night covered him with darkness, he saw a star. He said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "I like not those that disappear." And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people gone astray." And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with God. Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God." And his people argued with him. He said, "Do you argue with me concerning God while He has guided me? And I fear not what you associate with Him unless my Lord should will something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge; then will you not remember? And how should I fear what you associate while you do not fear that you have associated with God that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you should know? They who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice—those will have security, and they are rightly guided. And that was Our conclusive argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing. And We gave to Him Isaac and Jacob—all of them We guided. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good. And Zechariah and John and Jesus and Elias—and all were of the righteous. And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot—and all of them We preferred over the worlds. And among their fathers and their descendants and their brothers—and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path. That is the guidance of God by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with God, then worthless for them would be whatever they were doing. Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture and authority and prophethood. But if the disbelievers deny it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not therein disbelievers. Those are the ones whom God has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I ask of you for this message no payment. It is not but a reminder for the worlds." And they did not appraise God with true appraisal when they said, "God did not reveal to a human being anything." Say, "Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as light and guidance to the people? You make it into pages, disclosing some of it and concealing much. And you were taught that which you did not know—neither you nor your fathers." Say, "God revealed it." Then leave them in their empty discourse, amusing themselves. And this is a Book which We have revealed, blessed and confirming what was before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities <note>Mecca</note> and those</meta>

around it. And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers. And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about God or says, "It has been inspired to me," while nothing has been inspired to him, and one who says, "I will reveal the like of what God revealed." And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the floods of death and the angels are stretching out their hands, saying, "Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of extreme humiliation for what you used to say against God other than the truth and because you were arrogant toward His verses." And you have certainly come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left whatever We bestowed upon you behind your backs. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed that they were partners with God among you. It has certainly been severed between you, and lost from you is what you used to claim. Indeed, God is the splitter of the seed and the date stone. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is God; so how are you deluded? He is the splitter of the dawn and has made the night for rest and the sun and moon for calculation. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided 

<column-break/>

by them through the darknesses of the land and the sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know. And it is He who produced you from one soul and created a place of dwelling and a place of storage. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand. And it is He who sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby the growth of all things. We produce from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees—of its emerging fruit—are clusters hanging low. And gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar yet varied. Look at each of its fruit when it yields and at its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. But they have attributed to God partners among the jinn, while He has created them, and have fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe. Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing. That is God, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things. Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives all vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted. There has come to you enlightenment from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his soul.

<summary>This page contains verses 92 to 104 of Surah Al-An'am, discussing the consequences of lying against God, the reality of death and resurrection, and the signs of God's power in nature including the stars, rain, and vegetation.</summary>
<keywords>Qur'an, Surah Al-An'am, Day of Judgment, creation, nature, monotheism, jinn, enlightenment</keywords>

لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ ◦ مَا كَانَ

pages.translation:
such as "**your father**" and "**your brother**," provided they are not added to the daughters of the brother and their addition is to other than the first-person singular pronoun <term>Ya</term>. If they are added to the <term>Ya</term>, they are declined with estimated vowels on the letter preceding the <term>Ya</term>, such as: "This is **my brother**." They must also be in their full form <note>not diminutive</note>; if they are in diminutive form, they are declined by apparent vowels, such as: "This is **your little father**." They must also be singular; if they are dual or plural, they are declined as the dual or plural. The most eloquent usage for the word <term>han</term> <gloss>a thing/metonym for private parts</gloss> is the "deficient" usage, meaning the omission of its final letter and declension by vowels on the <term>Nun</term>, such as: "This is **your thing**," "I saw **your thing**," and "I passed by **your thing**."

<column-break/>

"I passed by **your thing**." For this reason, the author of the <term>Ajurrumiyya</term> and others did not count it among these names <note>the "six nouns"</note> and instead made them five. **As for the five examples**, they are every imperfect verb attached to a dual pronoun, such as "**they two do**" and "**you two do**"; or a plural pronoun, such as "**they do**" and "**you all do**"; or the second-person feminine singular pronoun, such as "**you [feminine] do**." These are raised by the stability of the <term>Nun</term> and made accusative and jussive by the omission of the <term>Nun</term>. **Observation:** It is known from what preceded that the signs of declension are fourteen: four are primary—the <term>Damma</term> for the nominative, the <term>Fatha</term> for the accusative, the <term>Kasra</term> for the genitive,

This substitution occurs in seven chapters: first, the chapter on the indeclinable noun; second, the sound feminine plural; third, the imperfect verb with a defective end; fourth, the dual; fifth, the sound masculine plural; sixth, the six nouns; and seventh, the five examples. <insert>Section:</insert> The three vowels are estimated

It is permissible for the **Particle of Attention** <note>ha al-tanbih</note> to precede demonstrative pronouns, such as "**Hadha**" <note>this</note> and "**Hatani**" <note>these two, fem.</note> and "**Ha'ula'i**" <note>these</note>. If the pointed-at object is distant, a literal **Letter Kaf** <note>kaf harfiyah</note> is attached to the end of the demonstrative word, which inflects as the pronominal Kaf usually inflects according to the person being addressed, such as "**Dhaka**," "**Dhakuma**," "**Dhakum**," and "**Dhalika**." It is also permissible to add a **Lam** before it, such as "**Dhalika**," "**Dhalikuma**," and "**Dhalikum**." This Lam does not enter the demonstrative word if it is in the dual form, nor in the plural form according to the dialect of those who use the long vowel; rather, it enters 

<column-break/>

in the second state of distance, such as "**Dhanikuma**," "**Tanikuma**," and "**Ula'ika**." Likewise, it enters the singular if it is preceded by the Particle of Attention, like "**Hadha**," so in the case of distance it is said "**Hadhaka**." For a **near place**, one uses "**Bi-hadha**" and "**Hahuna**," as in the verse: "**Lo! we sit here**" <note>Quran 5:24</note>. For a **distant place**, one uses "**Hunaka**," "**Hahunaka**," "**Hunalika**," "**Huna**," "**Hunna**," or "**Thamma**," as in the verse: "**And when thou lookest, then <note>thamma</note> thou wilt see**" <note>Quran 76:20</note>.

therefore, quite natural to find in the *sūtra* literature,
where the style of popular discourses is adopted, the
device of impressing upon the audience the mystic-
character of the Absolute by silence The Mahāyāna
*sūtras* do not tarry in characterising it as "unspeak-

cussion about the essence of the absolute is given in the
*Vimalakīrti-sūtra* The question is tackled from

to summarise, he remains silent, whereupon Bodhisat-
tva Mañjuśrī exclaims, "Well done well done, non-du-
ality is truly above words !".¹

Nor is this feature limited to Buddhist literature.
The Vedāntins resorted to the same device when
wishing to bring home the transcendental character of
their *advaita-brahma*. Śankara reports a case when
the question about the essence of *Brahma* was reiterated
three times without eliciting any answer.² At last,
when it was asked, "Why don't you answer ?" the
reply was, "I do answer (sc by silence), but you do
not understand me". Is it permissible to draw the
conclusion that Vimalakīrti and those men to whom
Śankarācārya refers had themselves no reasoned
opinion about the Absolute or that they were quite
indifferent and prepared to answer just as the ques-
tioner preferred, in the affirmative or in the negative ?³

It is asserted that a piece of cloth consists of threads. The cloth then could be a reality if the threads themselves had ultimate reality.<gloss>3</gloss> But they consist of parts.<gloss>4</gloss> They are themselves modifications of their own parts, they are no ultimate realities.<gloss>5</gloss> Therefore what is the use of maintaining that the result designated as a cloth consists of threads, when these threads themselves are no ultimate realities,<gloss>6</gloss> they are not "self possessors"<gloss>7</gloss> This has been expressed in the following aphorism,

> Cloth is existent in its threads,

तत्र अभावः अनित्यता वा भावमुपादाय प्रज्ञप्यते, खरविषाणादीनामनित्यतानुपलम्भात् । लक्षणमाश्रित्य लक्ष्यं प्रज्ञप्यते, लक्ष्यमाश्रित्य च लक्षणम् । अतः परस्परापेक्षिक्यां लक्ष्यलक्षणप्रवृत्तौ कुतो लक्ष्यं भावमपेक्ष्य अनित्यता भविष्यति ? तस्माद्भावोऽप्युपादाय प्रज्ञप्यते । ततो यदि अभावश्च निर्वाणम् , तत् कथमनुपादाय निर्वाणं भवेत् ? उपादायैव तद्भवेत् , अभावत्वाद्विनाशवत् । एतदेव स्पष्टयन्नाह— न ह्यभावोऽस्ति योऽनुपादाय विद्यते इति ॥

यदि तर्हि अभावः अनुपादाय नास्ति, किमिदानीमुपादाय वन्ध्यापुत्रादयोऽभावा भविष्यन्ति ? केनैतदुक्तं वन्ध्यापुत्रादयोऽभावा इति ? उक्तं हि पूर्वम्—

> भावस्य चेदप्रसिद्धिरभावो नैव सिध्यति ।
> भावस्य ह्यन्यथाभावमभावं ब्रुवते जनाः ॥ इति ।
-> [ म० शा०-१५.५ ] <-

तस्मान्न वन्ध्यापुत्रादीनामभावत्वम् । यच्चाप्युच्यते—

> आकाशं शशशृङ्गं च वन्ध्यायाः पुत्र एव च ।
> असन्तश्चाभिलप्यन्ते तथा भावेषु कल्पना ॥ इति,
-> [ लङ्कावतारसूत्र-२.१६६, १०.४५३ ] <-

तत्रापि भावकल्पनाप्रतिषेधमात्रम् , न अभावकल्पना, भावत्वासिद्धेरेवेति विज्ञेयम् । वन्ध्यापुत्र इति शब्दमात्रमेवैतत्, न अस्य अर्थः उपलभ्यते, यस्यार्थस्य भावत्वमभावत्वं वा स्यादिति । कुतः अनुपलभ्यमानस्वभावस्य भावाभावकल्पना योक्ष्यते ? तस्मात् न वन्ध्यापुत्रोऽभाव इति विज्ञेयम् । ततश्च स्थितमेव न ह्यभावोऽस्ति योऽनुपादाय विद्यते इति ॥ ८ ॥

अत्राह—यदि भावो निर्वाणं न भवति, अभावोऽपि, किं तर्हि निर्वाणमिति ? उच्यते । इह हि भगवद्भिस्तथागतैः—

> य आजवंजवीभाव उपादाय प्रतीत्य वा ।

# Chapter XXV: Examination of Nirvana

In this regard, non-existence—or impermanence—is designated in dependence upon existence, for we do not observe the impermanence of a rabbit's horns. The object to be defined is designated depending on the definition, and the definition is designated depending on the object. Therefore, in the context of the mutual dependence of object and definition, how can impermanence exist depending on the existence of the object? Therefore, existence itself is designated in dependence. Thus, if non-existence were nirvana, how could it be nirvana without dependence? It would have to be dependent, because it is non-existence, just like destruction. He clarifies this: "For there is no non-existence that exists without dependence."

If, then, non-existence does not exist without dependence, will things like the son of a barren woman be non-existences depending on something? Who said that the son of a barren woman is a non-existence? It was said before:

> If existence is not established, non-existence is not established.
> People speak of non-existence as the transformation of existence.
-> [MMK 15.5] <-

Therefore, the son of a barren woman does not have the nature of non-existence. And regarding what is said:

> Space, a rabbit's horn, and the son of a barren woman
> Are spoken of as non-existents; similarly, there is conceptualization in existents.
-> [Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra 2.166, 10.453] <-

In that case, too, it is only a refutation of the conceptualization of existence, not an affirmation of the conceptualization of non-existence, for the very existence of the entity is not established. "Son of a barren woman" is merely a word; no object is found, so it cannot be said to be either existence or non-existence. How can one logically conceive of existence or non-existence for an entity whose nature is not found? Therefore, it should be understood that the son of a barren woman is not a non-existence. Thus, it remains that there is no non-existence that exists without dependence. [8]

Here one asks: If nirvana is not existence, and also not non-existence, then what is nirvana? It is said: Here, the Blessed Tathāgatas have said:

> That which is the cycle of coming and going, when depending or conditioning,
> That, without depending and without conditioning, is taught as nirvana. [9]

"Cycle of coming and going" means the series of births and deaths. This cycle is sometimes designated as existing by relying on a collection of causes and conditions, like "long" or "short." Sometimes it is designated as arising, like the effect of a lamp,

<summary>This page discusses the dependence of all phenomena, including non-existence, and concludes that nirvana is defined as the cessation of the cycle of coming and going without dependence or conditioning.</summary>
<keywords>Non-existence, Dependence, Nirvana, Cycle of coming and going, Tathāgata</keywords>

while acknowledging that the first signs of that faith are to be found in As'vaghosha's treatise, yet make Nāgārjuna the first in their list of Patriarchs.¹

There is a great deal of uncertainty about As'vaghosha's life. His advent is said to have been foretold by Buddha himself, but Suzuki,² who has written a very full and candid account of As'vaghosha, quotes a passage from a book claiming to be written by Nāgārjuna, in which it is stated that, in order to fulfil all the prophecies concerning him, there must have been six As'vaghoshas, each of whom “appeared to fulfil his mission according to the necessity of the time, and there is no contradiction in them.” (Nāgārjuna's book was translated into Chinese in A.D. 401.) According to the first of these prophecies, As'vaghosha had been a disciple of Buddha in his earthly life. When the Buddha was telling his disciples of his approaching Nirvana, he had asked to accompany him, and then, “gazing at the pupil of Buddha's eye, had passed out of life.” In the next prophecy, Buddha is said to have told As'vaghosha that *three hundred* years after the Nirvana, he would obtain an inspiration from him which would be for the happiness of mankind. According to another, he was to come *six hundred* years after the Nirvana to confute the heretics. A fourth prophecy places him in the *eighth century* after the Nirvana; a fifth brings him back to *one hundred* years. A sixth represents him as having appeared to Buddha, seventeen days after his Enlightenment, in the form of a monster serpent with 86,000 heads and 86,000 tongues, and to have asked the Tathāgata 86,000 questions all at once. This sixth legend was evidently invented to bolster up the pretended revelations of the Kegon Scrip-

We read, *Bri. Up.* II, 3, ‘Two forms of Brahman there are indeed, the material and the immaterial, the mortal and the immortal, the solid and the fluid, sat and tya.’ The text thereupon divides the five elements into two classes, predicates of the essence of that which is immaterial—which it calls <term>purusha</term>—saffron-colour, and so on, and then goes on to say, ‘Now then the teaching by Not so, not so! For there is nothing else higher than this (if one says): It is not so.’ Here we have to enquire what the object of the negative statement is. We do not observe any definite thing indicated by words such as ‘this’ or ‘that;’ we merely have the word ‘so’ in ‘Not so, not so!’ to which the word ‘not’ refers, and which on that account indicates something meant to be denied. Now we know that the word ‘so’ (<term>iti</term>) is used with reference to approximate things, in the same way as the particle ‘<term>evam</term>’ is used; compare, e. g. the sentence ‘so (<term>iti</term>) indeed the teacher said’ (where the ‘so’ refers to his immediately preceding speech). And, in our passage, the context points out what has to be considered as proximate, viz. the two cosmic forms of Brahman, and that Brahman itself to which the two forms belong. Hence there arises a doubt whether the phrase, ‘Not so, not so!’ negatives both Brahman and its two forms, or only either; and if the latter, whether it negatives Brahman and leaves its two forms, or if it negatives the two forms and leaves Brahman.—We suppose, the <term>pûrvapakshin</term> says, that the negative statement negatives Brahman as well as its two forms; both being suggested by the context. As the word ‘not’ is repeated twice, there are really two negative statements, of which the one negatives the cosmic form of Brahman, the other that which has form, i. e. Brahman itself. Or else we may suppose that Brahman alone is negatived. For as Brahman transcends all speech and thought, its existence is doubtful, and admits of being negatived; the plurality of cosmic forms on the other hand falls within the sphere of perception and the other means of right

pages.translation:
<header>III ADHYÂYA, 2 PÂDA, 22.</header>

We read in the *Brihadâranyaka Upanishad* (II, 3): "Two forms of Brahman there are indeed, the material and the immaterial, the mortal and the immortal, the solid and the fluid, sat and tya." The text then divides the five elements into two classes, attributes qualities like "saffron-color" to the essence of the immaterial (which it calls <term>purusha</term>), and then says: "Now then the teaching by 'Not so, not so!' For there is nothing else higher than this (if one says): It is not so." 

We must inquire what the object of this negative statement is. We do not see any specific thing indicated by words like "this" or "that." We only have the word "so" in "Not so, not so!" to which the word "not" refers, indicating something meant to be denied. The word "so" is used here for proximate things, similar to the particle "thus"; for example, "Thus the teacher said." In our passage, the context points to the two cosmic forms of Brahman, and Brahman itself, as the proximate objects.

A doubt arises: does "Not so, not so!" deny both Brahman and its two forms, or only one? If the latter, does it deny Brahman while leaving the forms, or deny the forms while leaving Brahman? The <term>pûrvapakshin</term> <note>The opponent representing the opposing view.</note> suggests that the negative statement denies both Brahman and its forms, as both are suggested by the context. Since "not" is repeated twice, there are two negative statements: one denying the cosmic form of Brahman, the other denying the entity that has form—that is, Brahman itself. Alternatively, perhaps only Brahman is negated, because Brahman transcends all speech and thought, making its existence questionable, whereas the cosmic forms fall within the sphere of perception and cannot be negated. In this second view, the repetition of "not" is merely for emphasis.

who knows!—Not so, the pûrvapakshin replies. In the same way as sleep and the like, the departure of the soul is only referred to in the texts as something established elsewhere (not as something to be taught as part of true knowledge). Passages such as ‘When a man sleeps,—is hungry,—is thirsty’ (*Kh*. Up. VI, 8), although forming part of chapters concerned with true knowledge, mention sleep and so on which are common to all living beings, because they assist the comprehension of the matter to be taught, but do not aim at enjoining them specially for those who know. Analogously the texts about the soul’s departure refer to that departure only in order to teach that ‘that highest deity in which the heat of the dying man is merged, that is the Self, that art thou.’ Now that departure is (in other scriptural passages) specially denied of him who knows; it therefore belongs to him only who does not know.

To this we make the following reply. That departure which is described in the passage, ‘speech is merged in mind,’ &c., must be ‘common’ to him who knows and him who does not know ‘up to the beginning of the way;’ because scripture records no distinction. The soul destitute of true knowledge having taken its abode in the subtle elements which constitute the seed of the body and being impelled by its works, migrates into a new body; while the soul of him who knows passes into the vein, revealed by true knowledge, which is the door of release. In this sense the Sûtra says ‘up to the beginning of the way.’—But he who knows reaches immortality, and immortality does not depend on a change of place; why then should the soul take its abode in the elements or set out on a journey?—That immortality, we reply, is ‘without having burned,’ i. e. for him who, without having altogether burned nescience and the other afflictions, is about to obtain, through the power of the lower knowledge, a relative immortality only, there take place the entering on the way and the abiding in the elements. For without a substratum the prâṇas could not move. There is thus no difficulty.

It may be urged, again, that Brahman being the material cause of the universe, it lacks the characteristic of immutability But this is not the case It is Prakṛiti, Mâyâ, (Plato's Matter), which is really the material cause of the universe, while the causality of Brahman operates through the medium of Prakṛiti (S' 37).
