The word 'also' supplies the further reason why Kṛṣṇa Vâsudeva is to be worshipped, viz., the recollection in the Smṛti that the devotees of Kṛṣṇa have also attained the fruit of immortality.—27

If you ask, why then has Vâsudeva been celebrated as one of the vibhûtis, the author replies.

**वृष्णिषु श्रेष्ठ्येन तत् ॥ २ । १ । २८ ॥**

वृष्णिषु Vṛṣṇiṣu, among the Vṛṣṇis. श्रेष्ठ्येन Śraiṣṭhyena, by reason of superiority, pre-eminence तत् Tat, that i. e. celebration among the vibhûtis.

28 His celebration as a vibhûti is by virtue of his pre-eminence.—54.

The declaration of the vibhûtis is solely for the purpose of opening the eyes of the reader to the fact that it is to the Supreme Lord to Whom belongs all pre-eminence mentioned in such passages as 'Among the Âdityas I am Viṣṇu' (Gîtâ, x, 21), etc.; and so too in the case of Vâsudeva: also, the celebration of Vâsudeva among the vibhûtis is for the purpose of opening the eyes of the reader to this fact only that He is the most excellent one among the Vṛṣṇis.—28.

**एवं प्रसिद्धेषु च ॥ २ । १ । २९ ॥**

एवं Evam, similarly. प्रसिद्धेषु Prasiddheṣu, in regard to well-known incarnations च Cha, and.

29. And similarly in regard to well-known incarnations.—55.

'Similarly,' i. e. in the same way as in the case of Vâsudeva, it should be understood that devotion to the other well-known incarnations such as Varâha, Nṛsiṃha, Vâmana, Râma, etc. also produces mukti as its fruit owing to these incarnations possessing the characteristic mark of Brahman. Or, the aphorism may mean that 'similarly,' i. e., by means of their possessing the characteristic mark of Brahman, the idea of excellence only is to be formed in regard to the objects which have been recited as vibhûtis in such passages as 'Among the Rudras I am Śaṅkara' (Gîtâ, x, 23) etc. For it is declared in the Skanda Purâṇa (Kâśikhaṇḍa, Pûrvabhâga, xxxvii, 181).

"Whoever would declare the difference of Viṣṇu and Rudra, or between Śrî and Gaurî,
That utterance of the erring fool is repugnant to the Śâstra"

The proof of Śaṅkara's possessing the characteristic mark of Brahman is abundantly found in the Smṛti, etc.—29

Thus ends the first lecture of the second chapter in the Commentary on the One Hundred Aphorisms of Sâṇḍilya composed by the most learned teacher Svapneśvara.

भक्तिः पुनाति मन्निष्ठा श्वपाकानपि सम्भवात् ॥ ८६ ॥
( ११ । १४ । १९-२१ श्रीकृष्ण )

किञ्च भक्तस्य प्रायश्चित्तान्तरापेक्षापि नास्तीत्याह यथेति । पाकाद्यर्थं प्रज्वलितो वह्निः यथा काष्ठानि भस्मीकरोति तथा रागादिवासनापि कथञ्चित् मन्निष्ठा सती भक्तिः ॥ ८७ ॥

समस्तपापानीति । भगवानपि स्वभक्तिमहिमाश्चर्येण सशोधयति । अहो उद्धवति अत एवभूत श्रेयो नास्त्यन्यदित्याह न साधयतीति । न साधयतीति न वशीकरोति यथा भक्तिः साधयति अतएव ऊर्जिता योगादिभ्य उत्कृष्टा ॥ ८८ ॥

सर्वपावनत्वाच्चोर्जितेत्याह भक्त्येति श्रद्धया भक्ति तया । सम्भवात् जातिदोषादपि यत्र मद्भक्तो जातिचाण्डालत्वं जहाति तत्र कर्मचाण्डालत्वं जहातीति भावम् ॥ ८९ ॥

87-89 As the fire with its briskly kindled flames reduces fuel to ashes so does, O Uddhava, devotion to me consume all sins. Neither Yoga (Karma-yoga) nor Sânkhya (Jnâna yoga), nor the practice of ordinances (Vedic ritualistic rites) nor recitation of the Vedas, performance of penances nor deeds of charity wins me so much O Uddhava, as does devotion which is superior to all. Only one pointed devotion and faith am I won. I who am the very loved life of the saints. Devotion to me sanctifies even the feeder on dog's flesh (the Chândala the lowest of the social strata) and purifies him of the stain of his birth and vocation — XI 14 19-21 (Kṛṣṇa)

Note — Instances of members of the most depressed classes having been elevated into the rank of saints occur in the religious, especially Vaishnava, literature of the Hindus.

धर्म सत्यदयोपेतो विद्या वा तपसान्विता ।
मद्भक्त्या चेतसात्मानं न सम्यक् प्रपुनाति हि ॥ ९० ॥
( ११ । १४ । २२ श्रीकृष्ण )

भक्त्यभावे अन्यत्साधनं स्वनिष्ठमपि व्यर्थमित्याह द्वाभ्याम् । धर्म इति । विद्या उपासना आत्मविद्या वा आत्मानं अन्तःकरणं पुनाति नतु सम्यक् साशेषमित्यथ ॥ ९० ॥

90 The religion of truth speaking and of the practice of compassion, the learning that is associated with asceticism and penance—these do not sanctify the man who is devoid of my devotion—XI 14 22 (Kṛṣṇa)

Note — This may be a hit against the atheistic Bauddhas and Jainas whose systems of religion differ so much in essentials from the theistic Bhâgavatas.

कथं विना रोमहर्षं द्रवता चेतसा विना ।
विनाऽऽनन्दाश्रुकलया शुद्ध्येद्भक्त्या विनाऽशयः ॥ ९१ ॥

<header>THE FIRST STRING 89-91</header>

<note>original: "भक्त्याहमेकया ग्राह्यः श्रद्धयात्मा प्रियः सताम् । भक्तिः पुनाति मन्निष्ठा श्वपाकानपि सम्भवात् ॥ ८६ ॥ ( ११ । १४ । १९-२१ श्रीकृष्ण )"</note>

Furthermore, the text states that a devotee does not require any other act of atonement. Just as a fire kindled for cooking reduces wood to ashes, so does devotion fixed on Me consume even the latent impressions of desires. "All sins" refers to the fact that the Lord purifies even the greatness of His own devotion. There is nothing better than this. It does not win Him over like devotion does, therefore it is "superior" to Yoga and the like.—87-88.

Because it is universally purifying, it is called "superior." By devotion and faith, one is won. By birth, even if a devotee is a <term>Châṇḍâla</term> <gloss>the lowest of the social strata; an outcaste</gloss>, he abandons the stain of his birth. The implication is that he abandons the stain of his caste and the stain of his deeds.—89.

87-89 As the fire with its briskly kindled flames reduces fuel to ashes so does, O Uddhava, devotion to me consume all sins. Neither <term>Yoga</term> <gloss>Karma-yoga</gloss> nor <term>Sânkhya</term> <gloss>Jnâna yoga</gloss>, nor the practice of ordinances (Vedic ritualistic rites) nor recitation of the Vedas, performance of penances nor deeds of charity wins me so much O Uddhava, as does devotion which is superior to all. Only by one-pointed devotion and faith am I won; I who am the very loved life of the saints. Devotion to me sanctifies even the feeder on dog's flesh and purifies him of the stain of his birth and vocation.—XI. 14. 19-21 (Kṛiṣṇa)

Note — Instances of members of the most depressed classes having been elevated into the rank of saints occur in the religious, especially Vaishnava, literature of the Hindus.

<note>original: "धर्म सत्यदयोपेतो विद्या वा तपसान्विता । मद्भक्त्या चेतसात्मानं न सम्यक् प्रपुनाति हि ॥ ९० ॥ ( ११ । १४ । २२ श्रीकृष्ण )"</note>

In two verses, the text explains that without devotion, other means are useless even if one is established in them. Religion, learning, or knowledge of the self purifies the heart, but not thoroughly or completely.—90.

90. The religion of truth-speaking and the practice of compassion, the learning that is associated with asceticism and penance—these do not sanctify the man who is devoid of my devotion.—XI. 14. 22 (Kṛiṣṇa)

Note — This may be a hit against the atheistic Bauddhas and Jainas whose systems of religion differ so much in essentials from the theistic Bhâgavatas.

How can the heart be purified without devotion, without the hair standing on end <note>a sign of ecstatic devotion</note>, without a melting heart, and without the flow of tears of joy?—91.

<header>THE SEVENTH STRING 24 25</header>

ननु आत्मधधनात् धरान्तर मा वृणीत मोक्षेण किमपराद्धमिति चेत् न तत्पादसेवारसिकस्य तद्विरोधेषु विपयेष्विव तच्छून्ये मोक्षादपि वैराग्योचित्या दित्याह द्वाभ्याम् भोक्तृणपद्माख्यायेन । न वयमिति । हे सखि द्रौपदि साम्राज्य सार्वभौमपद स्वाराज्य पेद्र पद भोज्य तदुभयभोगमार्क । विधिवेन राजत इति विराड् तस्य भावो वैराज्य अणिमादिद्धिमाकमित्यर्थ । पारमेष्ठ्य ब्रह्मपदं आनन्त्य मोक्ष हरे पद तत्सालोफ्यं नतु कामयामहे । यद्वा पूर्वादि दिक्चतुष्टयाधिपत्य साम्राज्यादि चतुष्कम् । कितु एतस्य गदाभृत श्रीमत्सर्वसपदाभयपादरजे। मूर्ध्ना वोढु कामयामहे । तत्सेवामेव वञ्छाम इत्यर्थ । तत्कि पादरज एव काम्यते अत आह । भ्रिय कुचयो कुकुमस्य गधेन आद्य ब्रह्मदिसेव्यया श्रियापि सेवितत्वात् इति भाव ॥ २२-२३ ॥

> 22-23 We do not, O virtuous lady, desire for the sovereignty of the earth, or of the heavens, of the regions of Brahma, of Patal or even Moksa. But we do desire to have the blessed dust of the foot of the discus-holder (Narayana), the dust which is fragrant with the saffron of Laksmi's bosom — X 83 41-42 (The Queens to Draupadi)

को नु राजन्द्रियवान् मुकुदचरणाबुजम् ।
न भजेत्सर्वतो मृत्युरुपास्यममरोत्तमै ॥ २४ ॥

(११ । २ । ३ शुकः ।)

तस्मात्फलितमाह । शुकचाफ्येन को नु राजन्निति । हे राजन् परीक्षित इन्द्रियवान् अधिकलेंद्रिय । सर्वतो मृत्यु भय यस्य स । मुकुदचरणाम्बुज भजेत तस्यैव अभयत्वादिति भाव ॥ २४ ॥

24 O King (Pariksit) ! what person, that is in possession of his sense, would not worship the foot of Mukunda, adored by the greatest gods? Surrounded as that man is by Terror (Death) — XI 2 2 (Suka)

मन्ये कुतश्चिद्भयमच्युतस्य पादाम्बुजोपासनमत्र नित्यम् ।
उद्विग्नबुद्धेरसदात्मभावाद्विश्वात्मना यत्र निवर्तते भी ॥ २५ ॥

(११ । २ । ३३ कवि )

एतदेव कविवाक्येनाह । मन्य इति । न कुतश्चिद्भय यस्य तदकुतश्चिद्भयं तव अत्र संसारे असदात्मभावात् असति देहादौ आत्मभावात् भावनात् नित्य सर्वदा उद्विग्नबुद्धे विश्वात्मना सर्वथा निःशेष यत्र पदायुजोपासने भी निवर्तते तत् । तस्मात्स्वधर्मत्यागेनापि भगवत्पादसेवन कार्यमिति रहस्यम् ॥ २५ ॥

25 I consider that the worship of Achyuta (Visnu) should be the unceasing duty of man in this world. For distracted by divergent thoughts he identifies his spirit with his body. He gets rid of his fears by so doing (i.e., by his devotion to Visnu) — XI 2 33 (Kavi)

pages.translation:
<header>THE SEVENTH STRING 24-25</header>

<term>na vayaṃ sādhiṣa sāmrajyaṃ svarājyaṃ bhojyamapyuta |</term>
<term>vairājyaṃ pārameṣṭhyaṃ vā ānantyaṃ vā hareḥ padam || 22 ||</term>
<term>kāmayāmahe etasya śrīmatpādarajaḥ śriyaḥ |</term>
<term>kucakuṅkumagandhāḍhyaṃ mūrdhnā voḍhuṃ gadābhṛtaḥ || 23 ||</term>
(X. 83. 41-42. The Queens)

<note>The Queens of <term>Krishna</term> address <term>Draupadi</term>, explaining that they do not seek the sovereignty of the earth, the heavens, or the status of <term>Brahmâ</term> or <term>Pâtâla</term>. They only desire the dust from the feet of the Lord (<term>Gadābhṛta</term>—the discus-holder), which is fragrant with the saffron of <term>Lakṣmī's</term> bosom, to place upon their heads.</note>

22-23. We do not, O virtuous lady, desire for the sovereignty of the earth, or of the heavens, of the regions of <term>Brahmâ</term>, of <term>Pâtâla</term>, or even <term>Mokṣa</term>. But we do desire to have the blessed dust of the foot of the discus-holder (<term>Nârâyana</term>), the dust which is fragrant with the saffron of <term>Lakṣmī's</term> bosom — X. 83. 41-42 (The Queens to Draupadi).

<term>ko nu rājannindriyavān mukundacaraṇābujam |</term>
<term>na bhajetsarvato mṛtyurupāsyamamarottamaiḥ || 24 ||</term>
(XI. 2. 3. Suka)

24. O King (<term>Parīkṣit</term>)! what person that is in possession of his senses would not worship the foot of <term>Mukunda</term>, adored by the greatest gods? Surrounded as that man is by Terror (Death) — XI. 2. 3 (Suka).

<term>manye kutaścidbhayamacyutasya pādāmbujopāsanamatra nityam |</term>
<term>udvignabuddherasadātmabhāvādviśvātmanā yatra nivartate bhī || 25 ||</term>
(XI. 2. 33. Kavi)

25. I consider that the worship of <term>Achyuta</term> (<term>Viṣṇu</term>) should be the unceasing duty of man in this world. For distracted by divergent thoughts, he identifies his spirit with his body. He gets rid of his fears by so doing (i.e., by his devotion to <term>Viṣṇu</term>) — XI. 2. 33 (Kavi).

<summary>This page illustrates the surrender of the Queens to the Lord's feet and reinforces the necessity of devotion as a protection against the fear of death and bodily identification.</summary>
